messages:
maria-support: FYI — AcmeData on Dedicated is hitting a parsing failure with our Python SDK in "json-stream" mode. Error: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 123 (char 122)

dev-bot: Incident created INC-2026-142 :rotating_light:

oleg-eng: Can you paste the raw stream chunks and the SDK version? Also which model/route were they hitting?

maria-support: SDK v1.8.2 (python), route: /v1/generate?mode=json-stream, model: rwd-ggml-small. Raw stream (customer redacted ids):

```
chunk 1: b'{"id":"1","text":"Hello world","meta":{"lang":"en"}}\n'
chunk 2: b'{"id":"2","text":"This string has an escaped quote: \" and more'
chunk 3: b' text continued","meta":{}}'
```

When the SDK assembles chunks it tries json.loads(buffer) and crashes because the server split mid-string.

sam-py: I think this is the streaming parser bug we talked about — the Python client assumes chunks end on object boundaries. If a chunk splits inside an escaped sequence it will throw. We should buffer until we have a complete top-level object, but our current heuristic checks only for matching braces which fails for strings containing braces and escapes.

xia-ts: TS client had a related issue where chunk boundaries split multi-byte UTF-8 characters and TextDecoder threw. Different root cause but same class of problem. :eyes:

oleg-eng: Server change note — last week runtime started micro-chunking to reduce tail latency (split every ~256B). That can split inside JSON tokens. We need a framing protocol: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) or length-prefix each object, or guarantee server chunk boundaries align with token boundaries. Which is fastest to ship?

sam-py: Quick mitigation: SDK can switch to a tolerant buffering parser that keeps appending bytes until json.loads succeeds (with incremental checks) and only raise after a timeout or max buffer. I'll open a patch with tests.

maria-support: Customer repro steps I gave them (python):

```
import requests
import json
buf = b''
r = requests.get(url, stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=64):
    buf += chunk
    try:
        obj = json.loads(buf.decode())
        print('OBJ', obj)
        buf = b''
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        # keep buffering
        pass
```

This fails when decode() sees broken UTF-8 or an unterminated escape.

oleg-eng: That decode() before ensuring complete UTF-8 is the problem too. Use incremental UTF-8 decoding: 

```
import codecs
decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
text = decoder.decode(chunk)
buf += text
```

And only attempt json.loads when a full object is likely present.

ryan-ml: From the runtime side: we can toggle micro-chunking off for the Dedicated pool used by AcmeData while we fix the framing. We'll also add a flag to avoid splitting inside quotes by scanning the output stream state (inside_string, escape_next). Not perfect but buys time.

sam-py: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/384 — adds incremental UTF-8 decoder, resilient buffering, and a small-state parser that counts top-level braces but ignores braces inside strings using a simple state machine. Tests added that feed server-like split-chunks. Needs staging deploy.

xia-ts: I'll add an analogous fix to the TS client — use TextDecoderStream and a tiny state machine to avoid attempting parse mid-string. PR soon.

maria-support: Customer accepted temporary mitigation (turn micro-chunking off) and will test tomorrow. They also reported one more symptom: sometimes they got "invalid escape \u" errors when server split after a backslash. That matches splitting mid-escape.

oleg-eng: Action items:
- [ ] eng-runtime: add server-side toggle to stop micro-chunking for the affected Dedicated pool (ryan-ml)
- [ ] eng-runtime: short-term patch to avoid splitting inside strings (ryan-ml)
- [ ] sdk: ship python PR #384 to staging and cut a patch release (sam-py)
- [ ] sdk: TS follow-up (xia-ts)
- [ ] support: coordinate with AcmeData, confirm staging results and then prod rollout (maria-support)

dev-bot: Assigned INC-2026-142 to oleg-eng, ryan-ml, sam-py, xia-ts

sam-py: Quick note — long-term we should decide on a canonical framing (NDJSON or length-prefix). NDJSON is easiest for customers (one JSON object per newline), but length-prefix is more robust for arbitrary binary payloads. I'll open a design doc.

maria-support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer and post back with test results. :thumbsup:

oleg-eng: Once python patch is green in staging, let's keep micro-chunking disabled for 24h and then roll gradual changes. Closing loop in 48h.
